claims.statement: The interactive one-command release is `pnpm release:android-host` (root) / `node scripts/release.mjs` (host package); it is TTY-only and has three modes: `-i` interactive commit selection (default), `-c` custom changelog, and `-o`/`--overwrite` to repair an already-published Release without bumping the version, while the retired OTA flags `--web-only`/`--min-web` fail loudly instead of silently running a full release.

The product version source of truth is `packages/app-lynx/package.json`; `sync-android-version.mjs` reads it and rewrites `build.gradle` `versionCode`/`versionName` using `versionCode = major*10000 + minor*100 + patch` (minor and patch must be < 100), and the release flow bumps exactly `app-lynx/package.json`, `android/app/build.gradle`, and `packages/website/version.json`.

Release signing is configured in `android/app/build.gradle` to read `pictelio-release.keystore` (alias `pictelio`) and the `PICTELIO_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD`/`PICTELIO_KEY_PASSWORD` environment variables, and `validateReleaseSigning()` runs only when a release task is in the Gradle task graph, so debug builds never require the keystore or passwords.

The release APK build is a fixed step sequence — sync credentials, build the Lynx bundle with `NODE_ENV=production`, sync `main.lynx.bundle` into Android assets, then `./gradlew assembleRelease renameReleaseApk` — producing a single `pictelio-{version}-release.apk` because the only publishable build type is `release`.

The normal release flow runs six steps — check signing env, bump version + write changelog/version.json, build the APK, git commit + tag (rejecting unrelated workspace changes), `git push origin <branch> --tags` with 3 retries, and `gh release create` plus per-asset upload — and its catch handler provides step-specific rollback or manual recovery commands.

Release must run on the target branch (default `main`, overridable via `PICTELIO_RELEASE_BRANCH`, which switches branch check, divergence preflight, and push target together); it rejects pre-existing tags and, per ADR-0142, fails fast before the confirmation prompt when `origin/<branch>` has commits the local branch lacks.

The overwrite release (`-o`) probes the remote, plans an update to an existing non-draft Release whose tag equals `v{version}`, then backs up replaced assets, edits notes, and re-uploads per asset with failed-asset restore — without bumping the version, moving the tag, or creating a commit.

Release assets are uploaded per asset with concurrency equal to the asset count, a maximum of 3 attempts per asset with 1s/2s/4s backoff, and failure isolation; a TTY upload panel shows one row per asset and non-TTY degrades to event lines (ADR-0065).

The default release uploader is a Node native HTTPS uploader that bypasses the proxy, streams files, caches the release `upload_url` per tag, obtains its token from `gh auth token` without logging it, and implements clobber by deleting and re-uploading on a 422; `PICTELIO_UPLOADER=gh` restores the gh subprocess, and `probeProxyRouting` prints whether the run goes direct or through a proxy (ADR-0067).

`sync-credentials.mjs` reads `packages/app-lynx/credentials.json5` and generates the gitignored `io.pictelio.app.config.OAuthConfig` Java class (OAuth credentials, header disguises, endpoint URLs, timeouts, `MIN_WEBVIEW_VERSION`, and cache config), and must run before Gradle compilation.

The website landing page (`pictelio-website`) has two distinct operations: `scripts/deploy.mjs` (root `pnpm deploy`) only copies `packages/website/dist/` into an untracked `_site/` directory for local preview (and ignores the `--dry-run` flag that `pnpm deploy:dry` passes), while publishing is done by `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, which builds Astro, copies `packages/website/version.json` into `dist/`, and deploys the artifact to GitHub Pages with `actions/configure-pages` + `upload-pages-artifact` + `deploy-pages` on pushes to `main` touching `packages/website/**` or the workflow (plus `workflow_dispatch`) — serving `https://a1121611810.github.io/Pictelio` via Astro `site`/`base` with no `gh-pages` branch push, so the gh-pages instructions in `docs/release-checklist.md` are stale.

The Android host's minimum OS version is API 28 (Android 9.0), set by `minSdkVersion = 28` in `variables.gradle`, and with the WebView client removed in v6.3.0 there is no second engine to fall back to.

The release toolchain requires Node `>=22.22.2` (repo pins `24.18.0`) and pnpm `11.9.0` enforced by root `package.json` `devEngines` plus `engine-strict=true` in `.npmrc`, Java 21 for the Gradle build, Android SDK minSdk 28 / compileSdk 36 / buildTools 36.1.0, and an authenticated `gh` CLI, which the release flow uses for Release create/edit as well as for the default uploader's token.

Developer-side Pixiv/API traffic is expected to reach a local HTTP proxy resolved as `https_proxy` → `HTTPS_PROXY` → `http_proxy` → `HTTP_PROXY` → hard fallback `http://127.0.0.1:7897`; the rspeedy dev server binds `127.0.0.1` only and routes its `/pixiv-img`, `/pixiv-api`, and `/pixiv-oauth` proxies through that agent, while the emulator E2E path instead sets the device's global HTTP proxy to the host proxy via `ANDROID_E2E_HTTP_PROXY` (for example `10.0.2.2:7897`) and clears it on teardown.

No Pixiv, OAuth, or signing credential enters CI: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs only type check/lint, `pnpm test:all`, and `sync:credentials` plus `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest --no-daemon` with no secrets, the refresh token and AI keys live in the gitignored `packages/app-lynx/.env`, and the keystore/key passwords exist only in the releasing shell's environment.

`probeProxyRouting` mirrors Go `httpproxy` semantics for https uploads (HTTPS_PROXY then ALL_PROXY, with NO_PROXY forcing direct), and because a NO_PROXY domain entry matches the domain plus all of its subdomains the documented direct-fallback value is exactly `NO_PROXY=api.github.com,uploads.github.com` — writing `github.com` would also bypass the proxy for `uploads.github.com`; since the default Node uploader ignores proxy env vars, HTTPS_PROXY only changes behavior in `PICTELIO_UPLOADER=gh` mode.

`pnpm dev:android-host` (`scripts/dev-android.mjs`) is the debug install path: it syncs version and credentials, builds the Lynx bundle with `NODE_ENV=production`, syncs the bundle into Android assets, runs `./gradlew assembleDebug`, and installs `android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk` with `adb install -r`; there is no dev-server or hot-reload variant because the APK loads `main.lynx.bundle` directly from assets, so 'dev' only denotes the debug build type.

The signed release APK is produced at `android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/pictelio-{versionName}-release.apk` by a per-build-type `renameReleaseApk` task declared with `outputs.upToDateWhen { false }` (so a stale `pictelio-*.apk` cannot be published), and `sync-android-assets.mjs` copies `dist/main.lynx.bundle` plus mirrors `dist/static/**` (hash-named icon fonts) into the host assets with byte-size verification, clearing the destination first — a missing `main.lynx.bundle` is the historical white-screen failure mode.

The signing keystore must never be committed: `packages/android-host/android/app/pictelio-release.keystore` (alias `pictelio`) is ignored by both `packages/android-host/android/.gitignore` (`*.keystore`, `*.jks`, `app/release/`) and the root `.gitignore`, and passwords come only from the `PICTELIO_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD`/`PICTELIO_KEY_PASSWORD` environment variables; `docs/release-signing.md` remains the keytool/procedure reference but its build command, `app-release.apk` name, and paths still describe the removed WebView/Capacitor chain.

The optional AI changelog summarization step (`-i` and `-c` only, not `-o`) reads `PICTELIO_AI_BASE_URL` / `PICTELIO_AI_API_KEY` / `PICTELIO_AI_MODEL` / `PICTELIO_AI_PROTOCOL` from `packages/app-lynx/.env` (explicitly not the host package); any missing key means 'not configured' and the step is skipped with a warning, the protocol is explicit (`chat` → `/chat/completions`, `responses` → `/responses`), the default per-call timeout is 240 s, only transient failures (network, 429, 5xx, non-JSON, empty output) retry once while 4xx and timeouts fail immediately, and the step runs before the step-1 signing check.

Release step 4 rejects any `git status --porcelain` entry outside the three release files, so the untracked `_site/` directory left behind by the local preview `pnpm deploy` blocks an interactive release until it is deleted.

`transition-matrix.spec.ts` is the only android-e2e spec carrying the `@release-gate` marker: it is the ADR-0163 pre-release manual gate (3 Lynx rows after single-engine consolidation) that runs outside per-PR CI through `pnpm test:android-host:e2e`, and because the suite skips as a whole when the pinned AVD does not match, the operator must confirm from the suite-level skipped count or `--reporter=verbose` suite names that the gate actually executed.

Because GitHub Releases is the only distribution channel, the ADR-0163 staged-rollout replacement is publishing the tag as a pre-release for at least 3 days and then promoting it (`gh release edit <tag> --prerelease=false`); the release script's `gh release create` call does not pass `--prerelease`, so the marker is set as a separate operational step.

`BENCH_NAV=1` is a compile-time macro (`__BENCH_NAV__`) that enables the benchNav deep-link hooks used by device verification and E2E, and it must be injected across the whole build chain (`BENCH_NAV=1 pnpm build:android-host`) because the chain rebuilds the Lynx bundle — injecting only `build:app-lynx` is overwritten; the shipping chain does not inject it, and the native forwarding additionally requires `BuildConfig.DEBUG`, so the channel is absent from a release APK.

`PICTELIO_HOME_BLEED` is a build-time rspeedy macro (default on; only the exact value `0` rolls back to the old 64dp top bar) whose polarity has a single source of truth in `packages/app-lynx/homeBleedHeaderFlag.ts`; because it is inlined into the bundle a shipped APK cannot be toggled, so the release operator must check `env | grep PICTELIO_HOME_BLEED` before building and verify the artifact rather than trusting BUILD SUCCESSFUL.

Release builds contain no debug channels: the `pictelio_dev_*` intent extras (auto-login refresh token, force-R18, LLM endpoint seeding) and the native benchNav forwarding are gated behind `BuildConfig.DEBUG` and removed by R8 in release, and Lynx debug mode is enabled with `enableLynxDebug(BuildConfig.DEBUG)`, which is false in release.

Several pre-release gates recorded in `docs/release-checklist.md` are currently unenforced and must not be recorded as passed: the dual-engine QA transition checklist (R1–R4), the engine-degradation evidence matrix (both unexecutable after single-engine consolidation without a WebView engine to switch to), the night-mode walkthrough acceptance record (`docs/research/lynx-night-mode-walkthrough-acceptance.md`) which does not exist yet so its gate stays closed, and the former 'debug backdoor key must not be present in the APK' assertion which is permanently zero and therefore no longer detects anything — replacements are pending redefinition tracked in #805.

Release-adjacent verification outside CI includes device-side scripts that drive a real installed APK (`tests/android-e2e/tools/verify-translation.sh` builds with `BENCH_NAV=1`, refuses to test an APK older than the packaged sources, and asserts the translation request actually fired), `packages/app-lynx/scripts/verify-top-inset.mjs` which measures rendered top-inset magnitude against the platform status-bar inset with its verdict logic in `topInsetVerdict.mjs`, and `.github/workflows/sysbars-acceptance.yml`, a manual `workflow_dispatch` assertion gate that runs the system-bar acceptance matrix on an API 35/36 emulator on a GitHub runner.

Some verification scripts cannot run against the single-engine build as written: `packages/app-lynx/scripts/lynx-device-check.sh` and `lynx-flow-check.sh` still launch `io.pictelio.app/.MainActivity` and seed the removed `pictelio_client_kind` preference, and `tests/android-e2e/tools/verify-abort.sh` still pins flavor-era artifacts (`assembleLynxDebug`, `apk/lynx/debug/app-lynx-debug.apk`), whereas the launcher is `LynxActivity` and the only variants are the `debug` and `release` build types.

Release-script invariants are unit-tested under `packages/android-host/tests/unit/scripts/` and run by `pnpm test:android-host` (which feeds `pnpm test:all` in CI): the step table vs real pnpm scripts/Gradle tasks/APK path, branch and divergence preflight topologies, a subprocess test that retired flags are rejected before the TTY guard, uploader and clobber/error classification, proxy routing, the `planOverwrite`/`executeOverwrite` seams, `version.json` shape, AI summarization protocol, changelog truncation, git-ref helpers, and upload-panel formatting.
